Subject: Multi-region reserved GPU pool fallback & immediate steps

Hi Dana / Victor —

We detected a sudden saturation event in the us-west reserved GPU pool at ~08:58 UTC that affected several requests routed to your reserved capacity. Our serving layer triggered automated fallback routing to the us-east spare pool but a subset of requests experienced elevated latencies and a small failure rate during the transition window.

Immediate items we have in flight:
- We opened an ops incident and applied a temporary capacity uplift to your reserved pool to bring headroom back.
- We rebalanced cross-region routing to prefer local capacity for low-latency routes.
- Connor is collecting logs and latency traces; we will share an evidence bundle within the hour.

Next steps we need from you: please share any request ids or timestamps for requests you saw degrade (if you have them) — that will help us correlate logs faster.

Apologies for the disruption. We are treating this as priority P1 and will follow up with a detailed timeline and post-incident evidence package.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193

Subject: RE: Multi-region reserved GPU pool fallback & immediate steps (prelim RCA)

Ben / team —

Prelim notes after initial triage (08:58–09:12 UTC window):
- Root trigger: a mis-scheduled maintenance job that overlapped with a surge in tenant warmups; the maintenance freed capacity in one host group while autoscaler was in a transient cooling period.
- Fallback path mis-qualification: a small subset of requests were routed to model-quantized variants in us-east that had slightly different kernel selection; this produced queuing and delayed KV cache warmup.
- Impact: increased tail latency and ~0.6% transient 5xx correlated to queue timeouts.

Working actions: aggregated logs and KV cache traces saved to a bundle (building now). I will add correlation for Dana's request ids.

Connor
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

- Impact: elevated p95/p99 latencies and a ~0.6% transient 5xx.

What we attached:
- redwood-ops-log-bundle-20260918.tar.gz (cluster logs, kernel selection traces)
- fallback-routing-trace-20260918.json (request-level routing traces including rr-* ids)

We are also scheduling a follow-up postmortem meeting on Mon 21 Sep at 16:00 UTC to review the full remediation plan and longer-term changes (autoscaler policy, maintenance window coordination, and improved fallback qualification).

Please let me know if that time works for your team.

Best,
Ben

Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 16:48:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: Postmortem summary & action items (recorded)

Hi all —

Thanks for joining the postmortem earlier. Per the meeting recording and the remediation runbook, here is the concise postmortem and commitments we will deliver: 

1) Root cause (confirmed): a scheduled maintenance job in us-west that coincided with a warmup surge; autoscaler cooling prevented immediate re-provisioning; fallback routed a subset of traffic to a model variant with different kernel selection producing delayed KV cache readiness.

2) Short-term fixes (already deployed):
- Adjusted maintenance windows to prevent overlap with tenant warmup windows.
- Temporarily reduced autoscaler cooldown for reserved pools during known warmup times.
- Added pre-fallback warmup verification: before routing to an alternate model variant, verify KV cache presence or prefer capacity with warmed caches.

3) Long-term changes (roadmap, ETA):
- Autoscaler policy overhaul to include warmup heuristics (ETA Q4 2026).
- Fallback qualification enhancements with a small A/B rollout and metrics guardrails (ETA Q4 2026).
- Playbook for reserved pool maintenance that includes mandatory simulation of warmup traffic (ETA Q1 2027).

4) Customer remediation & credits:
- We will issue the proposed 20% credit for impacted reserved hours; billing will follow up with the finalized invoice credit within 7 business days.

5) Deliverables by Redwood:
- Full evidence bundle (uploaded) — drive link: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-evidence-BR4821
- Postmortem doc (PDF) and change ticket ids: RW-OPS-1298, RW-SERVE-1772
- Follow-up sync scheduled if BrightRetail requests deeper technical session.

Action owners: Connor (evidence & autoscaler traces), Karthik (maintenance window policy), Marissa (customer comms + credits), Ben (exec sponsor & billing coordination).

Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
